title: Module 07 — Durable state
text:
How the reference DurableRuntime works
HelloPico (domain)
      │
DurableRuntime
      │
   SQLite
On each invoke, state is written to SQLite.
DurableRuntime.reopen(db) simulates process restart with the same store.

title: Module 07 — Durable state
text:
Demonstration
from oe_pico_runtime import DurableRuntime

rt1 = DurableRuntime("/tmp/hello.db")
rt1.invoke("hello-pico", "hello", {"name": "One"})
rt1.invoke("hello-pico", "hello", {"name": "Two"})
rt1.close()

rt2 = DurableRuntime.reopen("/tmp/hello.db")
print(rt2.inspect("hello-pico").event_count)  # 2
print(rt2.invoke("hello-pico", "hello", {"name": "Three"}).event_count)  # 3

Release execution resources while keeping durable state

title: Module 08 — Multiple Pico identities
text:
Exercise
rt = DurableRuntime("/tmp/multi.db")
for _ in range(7):
    rt.invoke("alice", "hello", {"name": "Alice"})
for _ in range(2):
    rt.invoke("bob", "hello", {"name": "Bob"})
rt.close()

rt2 = DurableRuntime.reopen("/tmp/multi.db")
assert rt2.inspect("alice").event_count == 7
assert rt2.inspect("bob").event_count == 2
Isolation + persistence after restart is required.
